rows: Pigment = insoluble particle dispersed in binder. Dye = soluble molecule bonding to substrate.
What creates iron oxide's red color?
d-d transition + charge transfer in Fe³⁺ hematite — absorbs blue/green, reflects red
Why is lapis lazuli so intensely blue?
S₃⁻ radical anion charge transfer (not d-d) — high extinction coefficient in zeolite-like aluminosilicate framework
What's the key parameter for organic pigment color?
HOMO-LUMO gap of the conjugated π system — larger conjugation = smaller gap = longer wavelength absorbed = redder color
How do quantum dots produce different colors?
Quantum confinement — band gap increases as nanocrystal shrinks, so smaller = bluer, larger = redder
Organic dye precipitated onto inorganic substrate (Al(OH)₃) to make insoluble colored particle
Two chemical innovations: tube paint (1841, outdoor portability) + synthetic ultramarine (1826, affordable blue)
Why does binder matter for pigment color?
Refractive index match between pigment and binder affects transparency vs opacity; oil shifts apparent color
